title: Telemetry staleness & on-call handoff notes (metric ingestion lag runbook)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working runbook + handoff note for dealing with telemetry staleness / metric ingestion lag that causes SLO burn alerts and noisy pagers. Goal: give on-call engineers pragmatic steps to identify whether an alert is due to real user-impact vs telemetry pipeline failure, how to triage quickly, and short-term mitigations until a patch or config change is rolled out.

TL;DR (two-line):
- If multiple dashboards show identical flatlines starting at the same time, suspect ingestion or scraper outage.
- If only a single metric path is stale but downstream reports are fine, consider exporter/key rotation or label explosion in prometheus agent.

Quick detection checklist (first 5 minutes):
- Check alert payload: which metric and which job/instance labels are referenced.
- Open main telemetry health dashboard (Grafana: Telemetry Home > Ingesters & Exporters). Note "last scrape" timestamps.
- Query a sibling metric (same job) to see if entire scrape is affected. e.g. PromQL: rate(node_cpu_seconds_total[5m]) vs up{job="node-exporter"}.
- Check central ingestion lag panel: prometheus_remote_write_queue_peak_seconds and remote_write_failures_total.
- Confirm whether traces/logs still flowing (Lightstep/Datadog/CloudWatch) — if logs are present but metrics missing, stronger signal of metric pipeline issue.

Investigation playbook (ordered for speed):
1) Determine scope: global vs subset of services
   - Run: up OR count_over_time(up[1h]) grouped by job/instance. If many jobs show down/unknown simultaneously -> ingestion tier (frontline agent or remote_write) likely.
   - If only a single service: check exporter (kube-state-metrics/node-exporter) and collector pod.

2) Verify Prometheus targets & scrape status
   - Grafana panel or direct: GET /targets on Prometheus UI. Look for 'lastScrape' and 'lastError' for the relevant job.
   - Common quick fix: restart prometheus-scraper sidecar or the node-exporter collector pod if kube-target returns 502/timeouts.

3) Check the metrics-collector (ingester) tier health
   - Inspect remote write queue metrics: remote_write_queue_highest_samples_per_send, remote_write_retries_total.
   - If queue is growing and remote_write errors present => network or remote endpoint (long-tail overloaded TSDB).
   - Short mitigation: temporarily enable local retention -> keep service-level dashboards on a fallback Prometheus instance (instructions below).

4) Inspect recent deploys / config changes
   - Query GitHub + CI: any telemetry-config PRs merged in the last 30m-2h? (see linked PR in header).
   - Check Fleet/Helm rollouts: `kubectl get rollout -n observability` and `kubectl describe rollout <name>` for failure hooks.

5) If metadata/labels exploded (cardinality spike)
   - Look at prometheus_tsdb_head_series or custom cardinality gauges. If head_series jumps massively -> exporter bug producing high-cardinality labels.
   - Mitigate: apply relabel_config to drop problematic labels at the scrape job (use emergency relabel rule stored in /ops/telemetry/emergency-relabel).

6) Validate alerts themselves (false positives vs true signal)
   - Cross-check with user-facing metrics (request latency, error rates). If user metrics are stable, mute SLO burn alerts with a short silence and create ticket for deeper fix.
   - If user metrics also impacted -> follow service incident runbook (SLO burn -> Sev2/Sev1 escalation).

Common remediation commands (examples):
- Restart collector pod: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/prometheus-remote-write -n observability`
- Check prometheus targets: `curl -sS http://prometheus-observability:9090/api/v1/targets | jq .`
- Apply emergency relabel (example): `kubectl apply -f emergency-relabel.yaml -n observability` (file lives in repo: telemetry-config/emergency-relabel.yaml)
- Temporarily flip dashboard source: update grafana variable `datasource_fallback = true` to point to fallback Prometheus cluster (only do under PM/lead approval).

Pager etiquette & handoff bullet points (for on-call to on-call):
- When silencing, annotate the silence with: reason, start_time, expected duration, linked ticket (SRE-412), and what will be attempted.
- If you diagnose ingestion queue backlog, notify infra-messaging channel and Ops to check network/TSDB endpoints.
- Add one-line summary to the incident channel: who did what, is it mitigated, next steps. Example: "Mitigated: restarted prometheus-remote-write; queue draining; silenced SLO-burn alert for 1h; follow-up SRE-412".
- For handoff: leave open todos and the current best hypothesis. Prefer explicit ask: "Please try to patch exporter relabel if queue spikes again" rather than vague notes.

Escalation criteria (when to call on-call lead / pager team):
- If SLO burn persists > 30m after mitigation and user-facing latency/error rates are also high.
- If multiple ingestion clusters show sustained error rates (remote_write_failures_total > 5% for 15m).
- If head_series growth > 3x baseline in 10m and cannot be controlled by relabeling.

Temporary mitigations (do not left in place > 24h without ticket):
- Apply a silence to noisy SLO alerts (documented reason).
- Use the fallback Prometheus for dashboards.
- Add relabel drop rule to block high-cardinality labels until exporter patch.

Post-incident follow-ups (actions to create as issues):
- SRE-412: root cause analysis for 2026-01-18 ingestion lag (linked). Owner: Samir. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Telemetry hardening: add synthetic heartbeat metric for each ingestion cluster with alerting on delayed heartbeats (>2m). Owner: Leah.
- Runbook refinement: add quick copy-paste commands for common clouds (GCP v. AWS). Owner: Jordan.

Open questions & notes to self (for next retro):
- Why did remote_write queue not autoscale earlier? autoscaler logs show "no recent CPU pressure" but queue was growing. Possible telemetry mismatch in HPA target metric.
- Add end-to-end test that simulates exporter label explosion and validates emergency relabeling blocks cardinality.
- Can we wire a webhook to automatically create a silence when ingestion cluster reports 100% remote_write errors? Risk: may hide real outages. Discussion needed.

References & helpful links:
- Prometheus targets page: http://prometheus-observability:9090/targets
- Grafana dashboard: Telemetry Home -> Ingesters & Exporters
- PR that changed remote_write config earlier: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-config/pull/87
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SRE-412
- Slack thread for the incident: slack://channel?team=T12345&id=oncall-sre

Appendix: short example PromQLs useful during triage:
- Check if a job is being scraped: `up{job="my-service-exporter"}`
- Recent scrape errors: `increase(prometheus_scrape_series_added_total[15m])` (compare baseline)
- Remote write error rate: `rate(prometheus_remote_storage_send_errors_total[5m]) / rate(prometheus_remote_storage_send_samples_total[5m])`
- Head series: `prometheus_tsdb_head_series`

Notes (informal):
- This doc is intentionally freestyle: copy snippets into Slack when handoff.
- Keep silences short and annotated. We burned a few hours last quarter because silences had no ticket and nobody remembered why they were created.
- If you are unsure, ping @Ava or @Leah before muting production SLO pages.

Last incident snapshot (2026-01-18):
- 09:12 UTC: multiple SLO-burn alerts fire for search latency (alert references search_request_latency_p99).
- 09:14: oncall inspected dashboards: search_request_latency showed slight increase but not matching SLO-burn. Node exporter metrics flatlined across many clusters at 09:10.
- 09:18: restarted prometheus-remote-write, queue drained over 22 minutes, silenced SLO-burn for 1h.
- Follow-up: created SRE-412 to track permanent fix (root cause: misconfiguration in remote_write endpoint health-check that started rejecting writes after certificate rotation).

End.
